## Core Overview
- Primary Purpose: Master how CSS applies styles hierarchically, structures layout geometry through the box model, and controls element placement using CSS positioning schemes.
- Fundamental Themes: Specificity and inheritance in the cascade, box model dimensions and rendering, and positioning contexts (static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky).

## Key Concepts and Rules
- The Cascade and Specificity: Conflicts are resolved by importance (!important), specificity, and source order. Specificity weight is calculated as Inline Styles (1,000) > IDs (100) > Classes, Attributes, Pseudo-classes (10) > Elements, Pseudo-elements (1).
- Box Model Anatomy: Every element is a rectangular box consisting of four concentric layers from inside out: Content, Padding, Border, and Margin.
- Box Sizing Modes: 
  - content-box (default): Width and height apply only to the content area. Total width = content + padding + border + margin.
  - border-box: Width and height include content, padding, and border. Total width matches the specified width plus margin.
- Margin Collapse: Vertically adjacent margins of block-level elements often combine into a single margin equal to the largest of the two, except inside flex containers or with clearfixes.
- Positioning Schemes:
  - static: Default normal flow. Top, right, bottom, left properties have no effect.
  - relative: Positioned relative to its normal flow position. Space is still reserved.
  - absolute: Removed from normal flow. Positioned relative to the nearest positioned ancestor (non-static parent).
  - fixed: Removed from normal flow. Positioned relative to the viewport. Stays in place during scrolling.
  - sticky: Hybrid of relative and fixed. Acts relative until it crosses a specified scroll threshold, then fixes.

## Exam Takeaways
- Specificity Calculation: Expect questions asking to compare two CSS selectors and determine which rule overrides the other based on specificity scores.
- Box Sizing Math: Be prepared to calculate the exact rendered width and height of an element given explicit width, padding, border, and margin values under both content-box and border-box rules.
- Positioning Context: Remember that absolute positioning relies on the nearest ancestor that has a position value other than static. If none exists, it anchors to the initial containing block (viewport).
- Normal Flow vs Out of Flow: Understand that absolute and fixed positioning remove elements from the normal flow, which can cause them to overlap other content.
